doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Cannonball and Nat Adderley as people
summary: Cannonball was happy-go-lucky and friends with Batiste; Nat was the stable business one.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: What kind of guy was he?

Oh easy, happy-go-lucky, I mean one of the most beautiful cats I ever knew. And I got — he and Alvin Batiste was great friends. And me and Alvin was brother-in-laws you know, we’ve been brother-in-laws for fifty years now, so every time Cannon would come in they’d be cooking gumbo and all, and it would be party time when he’d come to town.
And Nat, you know, contributed a lot to the success of that quintet with his tunes.

Well Nat was more stable, and you know, he was more the other type than Cannonball. Cannon was just happy-go-lucky, let’s have some fun. But Nat was, you know, he was in the business part of it. But I wasn’t around Nat as much as that because Nat would be with another crowd when he’d come to New Orleans and Cannonball would be with us you know.
That’s a shame he went so early.
